sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *tan ... que*, *tanto ... que* and *de tal manera que* from B2 Unit 31: they measure how much, or in what way, something happened, and say what resulted. A planned capital that was built fast and then grew beyond its plan gives you plenty of "so ... that" sentences. Here they work on Brasília.

sections.title: Results in Brasília
rows: La ciudad se construyó tan rápido que se inauguró en 1960.
Llegaron tantos trabajadores que hubo que construir nuevos barrios.
La ciudad creció tanto que hoy vive más gente fuera del Plano Piloto.
verb + *tanto que*: grew so much that
Lúcio Costa trazó el plano de tal manera que los ejes forman una cruz.
*de tal manera que*: in such a way that

items.spanish: El Congreso es tan conocido que aparece en muchas fotografías.
items.english: The Congress is so well known that it appears in many photographs.

items.spanish: Había tanta gente en la inauguración que las calles estaban llenas.
items.english: There were so many people at the inauguration that the streets were full.

items.spanish: Niemeyer proyectó la catedral de tal modo que la luz entra por el techo.
items.english: Niemeyer designed the cathedral in such a way that light enters through the roof.

sections.content: *Tan* goes only before an adjective or an adverb and never changes. Before a noun use *tanto* and make it agree (*tantos trabajadores*). After a verb use *tanto*: *creció tanto que ...*.
